original_question: If every increasing order-bounded sequence in an ordered Banach space X has a supremum, does it follow that X is normal?
target_in_paper: Open Problem 3.2(1) in Section 3: the paper asks whether the existence of suprema for every increasing order bounded sequence in an ordered Banach space forces normality of the cone. This is posed immediately after Theorem 3.1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/2409.19768))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right quantifier pattern and the right implication: it asks whether, for every increasing order-bounded sequence, existence of a supremum forces normality. That is exactly the content of Open Problem 3.2(1), rather than the neighboring theorem on separable spaces. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/2409.19768))
missing_details: In the paper, normality is a property of the positive cone X_+, not of the Banach space in the abstract: X_+ is normal if there exists C > 0 such that ||x|| <= C||y|| whenever 0 <= x <= y. Saying simply "X is normal" is shorthand, but not fully stand-alone. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/2409.19768))
The ambient setting is a real ordered Banach space: a real Banach space equipped with a closed cone X_+ that induces the partial order. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/2409.19768))

The question concerns order-theoretic suprema in X: for each increasing sequence (x_n), the least upper bound sup_n x_n of the set {x_n} should exist in the order on X. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/2409.19768))

The phrase "order bounded" should be made explicit as meaning that the sequence is contained in some order interval [a,b]; for an increasing sequence this is the same as being bounded from above, but the paper states the problem using "order bounded sequence." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/2409.19768))

To stay paper-faithful, no separability assumption should be inserted. Separability appears in Theorem 3.1, but Open Problem 3.2(1) asks the question without separability. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/2409.19768))
To stay narrow, the conclusion should remain normality of the cone, not the stronger Levi-property conclusion from Theorem 3.1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/2409.19768))
refined_question: Let X be a real ordered Banach space with closed positive cone X_+. Assume that for every increasing sequence (x_n) in X whose range is order bounded in X (equivalently, contained in some order interval [a,b]), the supremum sup_n x_n exists in X. Must the cone X_+ be normal; that is, must there exist a constant C > 0 such that ||x|| <= C||y|| for all x,y in X with 0 <= x <= y? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/2409.19768))
justification: The draft clearly targets Open Problem 3.2(1), not a broader neighboring problem. The nearby context is: Theorem 3.1 proves that, if X is separable and its cone is normal, then the existence of suprema for every increasing order bounded sequence implies the Levi property; and Theorem 2.1 says that the Levi property implies normality of the cone. This is exactly why the paper then asks whether mere existence of those suprema already forces normality, even without assuming it. So the refined version should isolate that precise normality question, define the order-theoretic terms, and avoid adding separability or upgrading the conclusion to the Levi property. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/2409.19768))
